newsitem.title: HONG KONG: S&P assigns four Thai banks public info ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns four Thai banks public info ratings.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said on Monday it has assigned public information ratings to four Thai banks.
Public information ratings, a new service started by S&P late last year, are based on publically disclosed information and do not rely on S&P receiving access to the rated banks' management.
S&P said it has assigned Krung Thai Bank Plc an "A-pi" rating.
It assigned "BBB-pi" ratings to First Bangkok City Bank Plc, Siam City Bank Plc and Thai Military Bank Ltd.

The Thai banking system faces greater competition, lower profit growth and an escalation in problem loans, stemming from a recent downturn in the Thai economy and a decline in the property market, S&P said.

It said the business and financial risk of Thailand's banks continues to be closely tied to the health of the nation's economy, as shown by the reduction in balance-sheet growth due to the economic slowdown in 1995.
The most obvious result of the economic slowdown has been the deterioration in Thai bank asset quality, specifically in the area of total non-performing loans, the rating agency said.

S&P said the economic slowdown, combined with the progressive deregulation and liberalisation of the Thai banking market, has resulted in greater competition among market participants and thus a greater reduction in margins.

In addition, the operating expenses of Thai banks are increasing because of growing staff cost pressures and higher expenses associated with the development and distribution of new bank products and services, it said.
Thai banks also face pressures associated with a developing economy, in particular the management of strains placed on management, technical, operational and financial resources.

"Unless credit growth is tightly focused and disciplined, potential will exist for a significant increase in the problem loans should the economy experience a significant unexpected downturn," S&P said.
S&P said the active role the Bank of Thailand plays in ensuring the maintenance of a strong and stable financial system is a positive credit factor for the banks.

The rating agency said Krung Thai Bank's A-pi rating is based on benefits resulting from 60 percent ownership by the Thai government and the expectation that the government will have a strong moral obligation to support it, if necessary.
The rating also recognises the bank's occasional special role as a government tool for implementing and supporting government policies, S&P said.
First Bangkok City Bank's BBB-pi rating is based on the bank's recent solid operating performance, improved asset quality, solid capitalisation and favourable earnings outlook.
The rating also reflects the strong support the bank received from the Bank of Thailand following its asset quality problems in the early 1990s, S&P said.

Siam City Bank's BBB-pi rating is based on its strong and continuing support from the Bank of Thailand following financial difficulties in the mid-1980s and the expectation of continued support, if needed.
S&P also said that Siam City Bank's asset quality and profitability have improved over the past five years.
Thai Military Bank's BBB-pi rating reflects the bank's sound position in retail banking, improved profitability, satisfactory capital base and partial ownership by the Royal Thai Army, S&P said.
